clusters.root_cause: Every failure in this cluster unwinds through BillingCycleService.prorate called from chargeFor, and every message is a money comparison off by a fixed quantum: 0.01, 0.02, 0.50 or exactly 1.00. Mid-cycle upgrade and partial-month cases dominate. The pattern is a rounding/scale defect in prorate (a double or a HALF_UP/HALF_EVEN choice where a BigDecimal with an explicit scale belongs), not 23 independent assertion mistakes. It is not resolvable from the bundle alone because the deltas run in both directions (expected 279.55 got 279.56, but also expected 12.12 got 12.11) and two ProrationTest messages report a tolerance larger than the observed difference (expected 633.15 got 633.17, delta 0.101), so the tests' own tolerance contract is inconsistent.
clusters.proposed_fix: Pin the proration arithmetic to BigDecimal with scale 2 and one declared RoundingMode, then make the assertions in BillingCycleServiceTest, ProrationTest and InvoiceControllerTest agree on a single tolerance. Do not change prorate before the rounding policy is decided.
clusters.human_note: Billing needs to state the rounding policy for prorated charges (which RoundingMode, at what scale, and whether the whole-dollar deltas of exactly 1.00 are a separate day-count bug). That is a finance decision, not an inference. Also note: backend/src/main/java/com/example/demo/billing/ does not exist in this checkout and never has (git log --all over that path is empty), so the agent could not read prorate or run the verification command. Confirm the nightly job ran against the branch it claims before acting.

clusters.root_cause: All 14 failures unwind through UsageAggregator.bucketFor and UsageAggregator.rollup, and each message compares a per-day bucket total that is off by 0.01, 0.02, 0.50 or 1.00 (expected 491.6 records in bucket 2026-03-09 but found 491.62). The aggregator is accumulating a floating-point sum per bucket, so bucket totals drift with input order and record count. The messages also describe fractional 'records', which means the assertion text and the quantity being summed disagree about what is being counted.
clusters.proposed_fix: Accumulate bucket totals in BigDecimal (or in integer minor units) inside bucketFor/rollup and round once at the boundary, and correct the assertion messages to say cost rather than records.
clusters.human_note: Someone owning usage billing has to say what precision a daily rollup carries and whether the 0.50 and 1.00 deltas are the same defect as the 0.01 ones or a second bug in bucket boundary assignment. backend/src/main/java/com/example/demo/usage/ is absent from this checkout and from all git history, so neither the source nor the verification command was available to the agent. Shares a shape with c1 but a different symbol and module; kept separate because the root cause is not proven to be shared.

clusters.root_cause: CustomerExporter.row dereferences Customer.getPlan().getName() without a null check, so any customer whose plan is null throws NullPointerException and takes the whole CSV export down. The test names state the rule the source breaks: returnsACustomerWithoutAPlan, persistsACustomerWithoutAPlan, rejectsADeletedPlan. The domain confirms the rule is real: Customer.plan is a @ManyToOne on @JoinColumn(name = "plan_id") with no nullable = false (backend/src/main/java/com/example/demo/model/Customer.java:32-33), so a planless customer is a legal row. An NPE is never the correct expectation, so the source is at fault, not the tests.
clusters.proposed_fix: Guard the plan dereference in CustomerExporter.row, emitting an agreed placeholder for the plan column when customer.getPlan() is null instead of calling getName() on it.
clusters.human_note: The classification is not in doubt, but the fix is not purely mechanical: someone has to choose what the plan column contains for a planless customer (empty cell, "Unassigned", or the row omitted), and that value is consumed by whoever ingests this CSV downstream. backend/src/main/java/com/example/demo/export/ is also absent from this checkout and from all git history, so the agent could not read row() or run the verification command, which is the second reason it stopped short of agent-fix-now.

clusters.root_cause: The two sides of the /api/devices payload disagree on the SIM field name. Half the failures say 'expected sim_msisdn to be present, received undefined' and half say 'no such property "simNumber" in DeviceResponse' or 'expected <89014103211118510720> but was: <null>', and every one of them names DeviceController$DeviceResponse.from on one frame and components/devices-table.tsx on the other. The field was renamed on one side only. This checkout is a third shape again: DeviceResponse exposes sim_number (backend/.../controller/DeviceController.java:109), the entity property is simNumber (model/Device.java:25), the column is sim_number (Device.java:24), the web client reads device.sim_number (components/devices-table.tsx:48) and hooks/use-devices.ts declares sim_number on the response and simNumber on the request. Three names for one field across the boundary is the defect.
clusters.proposed_fix: Pick one wire name for the SIM field, then change every consumer in one commit: DeviceResponse, the TypeScript Device type in hooks/use-devices.ts, components/devices-table.tsx, components/device-form-dialog.tsx, and the device fixtures in the affected suites.
clusters.human_note: Renaming a field in a published REST response is a versioning decision, and any consumer outside this repo that reads the old name breaks silently. A person has to choose the wire name (sim_number, simNumber or sim_msisdn), decide whether the old name is kept as a deprecated alias for a release, and only then sweep the clients. The agent must not pick a side. Note also that DeviceControllerTest, devices-table.test.tsx and e2e/devices.spec.ts do not exist in this checkout, so the failing assertions could not be read directly.

clusters.root_cause: Nine assertions across two suites look for the priority label 'Urgent'. Seven fail with 'Unable to find an element with the text: Urgent' and two fail with 'expected "P1" to be "Urgent"', which proves the component now renders P1 where the tests expect Urgent. The rendered value changed and the assertions were not updated, so the expectation is stale rather than the code being wrong. What the badge should say is copy, though, not a rule: nothing in either test name states a business rule that P1 violates. This checkout shows yet a third label: components/tickets-table.tsx:59 renders {ticket.priority} raw, and SupportTicket.Priority is an enum (model/SupportTicket.java:10), so the current tree would render URGENT, matching neither expectation.
clusters.proposed_fix: Once the intended label is confirmed, update the expected text in tickets-table.test.tsx and ticket-detail.test.tsx to match the component, and add a single priority label map in components/tickets-table.tsx so the raw enum is not rendered.
clusters.human_note: Whoever owns the support queue UI has to confirm that P1..P4 replaced Low/Medium/High/Urgent on purpose. If it did, the tests are stale and the fix is a text update; if it did not, the component regressed and the fix is the opposite change. That is a copy and UX decision, so the agent stopped. Neither tickets-table.test.tsx nor ticket-detail.test.tsx exists in this checkout, so the verification command cannot be run here.

clusters.root_cause: windowEndsAtMidnight and the usage.spec.ts cutoff assertions compare against wall-clock time rather than an injected clock. Six of the seven failures expect 2026-03-14 and observe 2026-03-15, and the run started at 2026-03-15T02:00:00+00:00 (timestamp attribute on every testsuite in the bundle), so the suite crossed the UTC date boundary between building the fixture and asserting on it. The seventh is the same defect at second resolution: 'expected window to end 2026-03-15T00:00:00Z, received 2026-03-15T00:00:01Z'. Six of the 13 raw entries carry retries=1, so the runner already treated these as retryable. Direct retry evidence: 7 testcase entries in this cluster carry a retries attribute and one of them, usage.spec.ts 'returns the window end #87', passed on retry, which the rubric names as direct evidence of flake.
clusters.proposed_fix: Quarantine the cutoff assertions, then have their owner inject a fixed clock (Clock.fixed in UsageWindowTest, a pinned system time in usage.spec.ts) so the window boundary no longer depends on when the nightly happens to run.
clusters.human_note: Time-dependent and one case passed on retry, so it stays out of production source per the rubric. The test owner has to decide the fixed instant these assertions should pin, which is a fixture design choice. Skip or quarantine the four UsageWindowTest cutoff cases and the three usage.spec.ts cutoff cases for now and re-run; do not change the aggregation code on the strength of this cluster.

clusters.signature: lengthMismatch|shared table fixture|row count off by one
clusters.root_cause: Twelve distinct tests in customers-table.test.tsx and usage-table.test.tsx each find exactly one row more than they expect (25 where 24 is expected, 27 where 26 is expected). Every stack in the cluster interleaves frames from both files: a customers-table.test.tsx frame appears inside a usage-table test and the reverse, which cannot happen unless the two suites share mutable module state, and the two suites also interleave by test index (74, 75, 76, 77...), so they ran together. Eight of the 20 raw entries carry retries=1. The signature is a shared fixture that one suite appends a row to and the other then counts, not an independent bug in either table. Direct retry evidence: 12 testcase entries in this cluster carry a retries attribute and four of them passed on retry (usage-table.test.tsx 'validates the page window #74', customers-table.test.tsx 'excludes the page window #77', 'paginates the page window #83', 'returns the page window #85'), which the rubric names as direct evidence of flake and rules out a deterministic off-by-one in the components.
clusters.proposed_fix: Quarantine the row-count assertions in both suites, then have their owner give each suite its own fixture (build the row array per test, or reset the shared module in beforeEach) so the counts stop depending on execution order.
clusters.human_note: Four of these cases passed on retry, so a deterministic pagination off-by-one is ruled out; the test owner still confirms by running each suite alone, which should pass. Held at quarantine-and-retry rather than a source change because the cross-file stack frames and the retry markers point at order dependence, and the rubric forbids touching production source on a flake. The current checkout supports the shared-state reading: __tests__/components/customers-table.test.tsx contains no row-count assertion at all, components/usage-table.tsx contains no pagination, and usage-table.test.tsx does not exist here, so these assertions did not come from this tree.

clusters.root_cause: The internal Maven mirror returned HTTP 503 for spring-boot-starter-web 4.0.0, so Gradle could not resolve :compileClasspath and :compileJava failed before any code was compiled or any test ran. The log is explicit: "Could not HEAD 'https://artifacts.internal.example.com/maven2/.../spring-boot-starter-web-4.0.0.pom' > Received status code 503 from server: Service Unavailable" (nightly-triage/bundle/logs/rc-artifact-registry-503.txt). This job produced no JUnit XML, which is consistent with failing at dependency resolution.
clusters.proposed_fix: No code change. Restore or fail over the artifacts.internal.example.com mirror and re-run the job.
clusters.human_note: For the platform team that owns the artifact mirror: the nightly pool cannot resolve Spring Boot from artifacts.internal.example.com. Confirm the mirror is healthy, decide whether the nightly should fall back to a public repository or a local cache, and re-run. Nothing in this repository can be changed to make this job pass.

clusters.root_cause: The self-hosted nightly runner filled its root volume, so Playwright could neither write a trace nor find its browser binary. The log shows "ENOSPC: no space left on device, write '/home/runner/.cache/ms-playwright/traces/trace-0041.zip'", "browserType.launch: Failed to launch chromium because executable doesn't exist" and df reporting /dev/root at 73G used of 73G, 100% (nightly-triage/bundle/logs/rc-runner-disk-full.txt). No test executed, so no JUnit XML was produced. Separate root cause from c8: a full disk on the runner, not an unreachable registry.
clusters.proposed_fix: No code change. Reclaim disk on the nightly pool (prune Playwright trace and browser caches, Docker layers, old workspaces) and cap trace retention.
clusters.human_note: For the platform team that owns the self-hosted 'nightly' pool: /dev/root is at 100% on the runner, which is why chromium is missing rather than any change in this repository. Decide the cache retention and cleanup policy for ms-playwright traces, then re-run. Do not treat the missing chromium as a Playwright configuration bug.

clusters.root_cause: :spotlessJavaCheck failed with format violations in four Java sources (billing/BillingCycleService.java, usage/UsageAggregator.java, export/CustomerExporter.java, controller/DeviceController.java) and the log states the remedy itself: "Run 'gradlew :spotlessApply' to fix these violations" (nightly-triage/bundle/logs/rc-spotless-drift.txt). No test failed for this reason and no behavior is involved. Spotless is really configured here: backend/build.gradle:6 applies com.diffplug.spotless 7.0.4, :83 configures it, and :141 registers formatCheck depending on spotlessCheck.
clusters.proposed_fix: Run 'cd backend && ./gradlew spotlessApply' on the nightly checkout and commit only the formatter's output. No rule is suppressed or reconfigured.
